extracted.intended_audience: Marine Corps / DoD contracting officers and acquisition professionals involved in OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting, managing, and evaluating OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing (outsourcing) studies for DoD installation support services, including required study steps, definitions, risk management, and program management recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required steps in an A-76 study
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular describes the steps that must be taken in an A-76 study, to include: Development of a Performance Work Statement; Conduct of a Management study to develop the Government's Most Efficient Organization; Development of the in-house Government cost estimate; Conduct of a Cost Comparison between the MEO and lowest priced responsible and responsive bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four elements form the procedural core of an A-76 competitive sourcing action and should be followed per Circular A-76 and its Supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Work Statement is a statement of the technical, functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed, identifies essential functions to be performed, determines performance factors, including the location of the work, the units of work, the quantity of work units, and the quality and timeliness of the work units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PWS serves as the scope of work and is the basis for all costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form; development of a sound and comprehensive PWS 'ranks at the top of the list' of factors dictating success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan is the document that outlines the changes that will result in the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) to perform a commercial activity in-house. The MEO refers to the Government's in-house organization to perform a commercial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Management Plan provides staffing patterns and operating procedures that serve as a baseline for in-house cost estimates; the MEO is the basis for all Government costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form and is based upon the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost comparison is the process whereby the estimated cost of Government performance of a commercial activity is formally compared, in accordance with the principles and procedures of this Circular and Supplement, to the cost of performance by commercial or ISSA sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons should compare the Government MEO estimate to commercial/ISSA bids (typically the lowest priced responsible and responsive bidder) following Part II procedures to assure equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measures provide a series of indicators, expressed in qualitative, quantitative or other tangible terms, that indicate whether current performance is reasonable and cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measures can include workload and output-to-cost ratios, transaction ratios, error rates, consumption rates, inventory fill rates, timeliness measures, completion and back order rates, quality service measures (responsiveness rates, user satisfaction rates), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A performance standard reflects the minimum, sector-specific, Federal requirement for the performance of a commercial activity. It incorporates both quality measures and cost measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost measures reflect the cost comparability procedures of Part II of the Supplement to assure equity in the comparison of performance standards with private industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO Performance Review
rubrics_metrics.description: When services are performed in-house as a result of a cost comparison, a formal review and inspection of the MEO should be conducted, typically following the end of the first full year of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-MEO Performance Reviews confirm implementation in accordance with the Transition Plan, establish the MEO's ability to perform the services of the PWS, and confirm that actual costs are within the estimates contained in the in-house cost estimate; adjustments may be made for formal mission or scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Value / Award on Overall Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Value -- The expected outcome of an acquisition that, in the Government's estimation, provides the greatest overall benefit in response to the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: OMB Circular A-76 should be amended to allow capture and incorporation of past performance data into evaluation criteria and to give contracting officers latitude to evaluate past performance, technical approaches, management plans, and award contracts to organizations providing the 'best overall value' rather than strictly lowest price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past Performance as an evaluation factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Past Performance — Information related to contractor performance on previous contracts for similar activities or services, with a focus on the ability of the contractor to meet cost, schedule and performance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB/Supplement recommends capturing past performance data on commercial activities and allowing its incorporation into evaluation criteria for contract awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Surveillance is the method by which Federal employees will supervise in-house or contract performance to ensure that the standards of the PWS are met within the costs bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveillance mechanisms must be established to verify contractor or MEO compliance with PWS standards and contract cost constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands must identify risks associated with A-76 studies; many commands failed to identify risks beyond employee reactions. Risks noted include incomplete capture of work in the PWS, selecting contract types that don't meet customer needs, unauthorized changes to the contract by Marines working near contractors, protests, contract cancellation, schedule slippages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk management should be applied consistently across the contracting community. Program managers should identify risk areas that could cause schedule slippage and take action to manage and mitigate risks; communication among contracting officer, A-76 program office, installation commander and customer is critical to manage risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management approach for conducting A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, installation commanders should adopt a program management approach mirroring major weapon systems development and procurement: designate a program manager and empower that person with broad authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a quasi program office for A-76 studies to create unity of command, assign one individual responsible for all competitive sourcing studies, establish study timelines, program metrics for tracking progress, sole authority to approve deviations, identify and mitigate risks. Example tracking method: modified Earned Value Management System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized database of best practices and lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Defense should establish and maintain a database accessible through the Internet containing information on lessons learned from completed A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database should be resident within the Acquisition Web homepage, services should be required to submit input at the end of each completed study, and primary focus should be A-76 study management and contracting issues, including best practices on developing PWSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver procedures for mission-critical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiver procedures to OMB A-76 should be established which installation commanders can use to protect commercial activities they deem mission critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers permit tailoring competitive sourcing studies to current installation conditions when justified; FAIR Act consolidation of commercial activities may affect decision authority but installation-level waivers increase local flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption is a determination, made in accordance with Circular A-76 and this Supplement, that a commercial activity may be converted to or from in-house, contract or ISSA performance, without cost comparison and may be justified by reasons other than cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions are allowable under defined circumstances and must follow Circular A-76 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and boundaries of Inherently Governmental Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: An inherently governmental activity is one that is so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Federal employees. Activities meeting these criteria are not subject to Circular A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C lists examples (control of prosecutions; command of military forces; conduct of foreign relations; determination of agency policy; selection/award/administration/termination of contracts; approval of FOIA responses; approval of licensing actions; control of treasury accounts; etc.) to be retained in-house and not outsourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Activity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial activity is the process resulting in a product or service that is or could be obtained from a private sector source. Agency missions may be accomplished through commercial facilities and resources, Government facilities and resources or mixes thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames which functions are appropriate for conversion/competition under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Administration vs. Commercial Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract Administration includes those inherently governmental activities performed by warranted contracting officers (CO), the contracting officer's technical representatives (COTR), and related payment evaluation staff. Contract administration is not to be confused with contract quality control, performance evaluation or inspection, which are defined as commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation: certain administration functions must remain in-house (government employees) while quality control/performance oversight may be treated as commercial activities under the Supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core capability retention
rubrics_metrics.description: A core capability is a commercial activity operated by a cadre of highly skilled employees, in a specialized technical or scientific development area, to ensure that a minimum capability is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core capability does not include skills, functions or FTEs that may be retained in-house for reasons of National Defense, military mobilization, security, rotational necessity, patient care, or R&D as provided in Part I, Chapter 1 of the Supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date definitions for studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Start date: (1) the date when a cost comparison begins (generally when a local Study Team is formed and actual work on PWS, Management Plan, and in-house estimate begins); (2) may refer to the actual date work is scheduled to begin under a contract as provided in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear definition of start date is required for uniform application of study timelines and schedule tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of commercial activities (scope guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix B provides detailed examples of activities considered commercial (audiovisual products and services, automatic data processing, food services, health services, industrial shops, maintenance/repair/testing, management support services, manufacturing, office/admin services, printing, real property, security, systems engineering, transportation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to determine whether an installation support function falls within commercial activity scope under A-76; absence from the list does not preclude commercial nature but provides common examples.
